sentence_stem: Anna's phone was switched off all day, so
correct_completion: she must have been somewhere without a signal.
full_sentence: Anna's phone was switched off all day, so she must have been somewhere without a signal.
acceptable_variants: she must have been out of network coverage.
she was probably travelling in an area with no signal.

options.text: she should have answered the phone yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This criticises a past action rather than speculating about the reason the phone was switched off.

options.text: she can be at home now.
options.why_wrong: This makes a claim about her present location, but it does not explain why the phone was off all day.

options.text: she must have been somewhere without a signal.
she would have called us back.
options.why_wrong: This describes a hypothetical result, not a logical explanation for the phone being switched off.

grammar_focus: Modal perfect 'must have + past participle' for speculation about a past event
explanation: The connector 'so' introduces a logical result of the first clause. The modal perfect 'must have been' expresses a confident conclusion about a past situation. Ukrainian speakers may be tempted to use a simple past form here, because Ukrainian has no direct equivalent of the English modal perfect.
translation: Телефон Анни був вимкнений увесь день, тож, мабуть, вона була десь, де немає зв'язку.
